mbm-0468.clue: My paddle has a postcard on its handle.
mbm-0468.quote: I wrapped a little sketch of our favorite cove beneath the clear tape on my canoe paddle. When fog hid the cove I could still see the bright red cabin under my thumb.

mbm-0469.clue: I kept a slice for the sign painter.
mbm-0469.quote: The fair’s pie contest had a beautiful painted cherry on its sign. After the judging I saved the last slice for the person who painted it. She left one red brushstroke on my paper plate.

mbm-0470.clue: I saved a place for the empty reel.
mbm-0470.quote: At our little cinema the projectionist sets the empty reel on a blue stool during the changeover. I got to hold it once. It was warm, and suddenly the whole film seemed to fit in my hands.

mbm-0471.clue: I bring the chalk to the practice mat.
mbm-0471.quote: My first martial-arts teacher drew a small arc on the floor to show me the turn. Now I draw it for my little sister. She made one very neat arc and added a chalk rainbow on top.

mbm-0472.clue: I left the whistle on the towel.
mbm-0472.quote: At the outdoor onsen I heard a meadow bird through the steam and tried to whistle back. It answered only when I stopped. I spent the rest of the bath listening and got a whole concert.

mbm-0473.clue: I trained for the blue hour.
mbm-0473.quote: Our outdoor pool opens just before dawn twice a summer. I swam one length while the water was still dark blue and came back through pink reflections. I wish the lane were twice as long.

mbm-0474.clue: I kept the little patch of maple.
mbm-0474.quote: I slipped on a sliver from our alley’s old lane when they replaced the floor. The owner sanded it into a small key ring for me. My pocket now carries one inch of my very first strike.

mbm-0475.clue: I throw gently near the red flowers.
mbm-0475.quote: Our frisbee game has a flowerbed that counts as a lake. The first time my throw landed beside the roses, my sister made the winner water the whole bed. The roses have flourished under this rule.

mbm-0476.clue: I keep an extra knot in my pocket.
mbm-0476.quote: I practiced a disappearing knot so long my younger cousin asked where all the vanished knots go. I tied a spare in a piece of blue cord and handed it over. She checks on it after every show.

mbm-0477.clue: I didn’t know a raft could carry a tune.
mbm-0477.quote: We paddled under the old railway viaduct and somebody tapped the tube with a paddle handle. Each arch sent back a different drumbeat. We floated beneath the last one twice to hear it again.

mbm-0478.clue: I made a pocket for the healer.
mbm-0478.quote: My fantasy deck has one healer card that has survived three different decks. I stitched a little pocket for it in the deck bag. Whatever monsters I bring home, somebody has to look after them.

mbm-0479.clue: I programmed a fish to wait for supper.
mbm-0479.quote: My little screen fish swims in circles until somebody presses the space bar to feed it. My dad presses so carefully he lifts his finger afterward to see if a crumb is missing.

mbm-0480.clue: I watch the windows more than the wheels.
mbm-0480.quote: On the evening train the dining car windows glow a shade warmer than the rest. I drew one small square in gold and the next in blue until my notebook looked like a traveling city.

mbm-0481.clue: I had the ball, but my mother had the shoes.
mbm-0481.quote: For a lucky game at the alley I let Mum tie the laces as she did when I was small. She tied one very serious double knot, then bowled the first strike herself. I should have asked for her ball too.

mbm-0482.clue: I use the tin lid to look at the stars.
mbm-0482.quote: At camp I polished a biscuit-tin lid until my niece could see the moon in it. She carried that small moon through the tent flap to show her dad. For a moment the whole tent had a skylight.

mbm-0483.clue: I still have the usher’s pencil.
mbm-0483.quote: Our local cinema hosted a silent film with live piano. I borrowed a pencil to sketch the pianist’s hands and forgot to give it back. The usher wrote me a little ticket for one return visit.

mbm-0484.clue: I pick a book by its first sound.
mbm-0484.quote: I read the first sentence quietly to myself in the shop. A story that started with the sound of a latch followed me all the way to the till. I kept listening for that door to open.

mbm-0485.clue: I put chalk on the handles of a suitcase.
mbm-0485.quote: My gym partner laughed at the little chalky grips I’d left on my travel case. It’s what I carried the first pairs of weights in when we had nowhere to train. She helped me keep the old handle.

mbm-0486.clue: I wanted a garden I could keep on a floppy disk.
mbm-0486.quote: I wrote a little program that plants a pixel flower every time a friend visits and types their name. The field is getting crowded. I added a tiny watering can so it would look like I knew what I was doing.

mbm-0487.clue: I put my sister’s freckles in the polka dots.
mbm-0487.quote: I made a quilted portrait from fabric scraps and kept the dotted cloth for her cheeks. She counted the spots, then drew one tiny extra freckle on my cheek to even things up.

mbm-0488.clue: I punched the last hole with the lights out.
mbm-0488.quote: I made a leather collar for our old toolbox so the lid would close quietly. The power went out before I could finish. Dad held the lantern and I put the last brass rivet through its little ring of light.

mbm-0489.clue: I prefer the contest with the small plates.
mbm-0489.quote: At the mandu contest my sister hands me one dumpling on each little saucer. I know how far I’ve gone by the stack of blue dishes. She’s already planned what to build with the tower afterward.

mbm-0490.clue: I let the buttons tell the time.
mbm-0490.quote: I sewed a clock face into the quilt for my father’s armchair. Twelve different buttons are the hours. He’s always pointing its fabric hands toward teatime, and I’m happy to oblige.

mbm-0491.clue: I made a tunnel out of the sky.
mbm-0491.quote: I built a mini-golf hole inside a shoebox painted dark blue, with tiny pinholes in the roof. Roll the ball through on a sunny day and it travels under a sky full of afternoon stars.

mbm-0492.clue: I can bring the sunset back to the landing.
mbm-0492.quote: I painted the underside of my canoe paddle peach because it matched the water on my first evening trip. When I raise it to wave from shore, my sister says the sunset has waved back.
